questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Present perfect and the simple past
questions.learningObjective: Choose the tense for a recent completed action
questions.stem: A city planner writes: 'We ___ the zoning report yesterday.' Which tense fits a completed past action?

options.misconception: uses present perfect for a finished past time
uses progressive for a completed action
uses pluperfect without a prior reference

questions.explanation: A specific past time ('yesterday') calls for the simple past. Present perfect would leave the time open.
questions.hint: Check whether the time is finished.

provenance.author: bank-team-spanish
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.stem: Explain when a planner should use the present perfect rather than the imperfect in a memo.

answer.exemplar: Use the present perfect for a recent action with present relevance; use the imperfect for ongoing or habitual background description.

questions.explanation: The present perfect looks back at a completed action that still matters now. The imperfect paints background or habit.
questions.hint: Ask whether the action still matters now.

provenance.author: bank-team-spanish
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Use desde with the present tense

stimulus.body: Memo line: 'The plaza has been closed ___ Monday.' Need: a Spanish rendering that keeps the duration sense.

questions.stem: Which Spanish rendering keeps the duration sense of 'since Monday'?

options.text: 'La plaza está cerrada desde el lunes.'

options.misconception: drops the duration and marks a single closure
uses a passive past, losing the ongoing state

questions.explanation: Option A keeps 'desde' with a present state, expressing duration. The others mark a one-off closure or habit.

provenance.author: bank-team-spanish
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.stem: Write a sentence stating that a road was closed for two weeks as a completed stretch.

answer.exemplar: La carretera estuvo cerrada durante dos semanas.

questions.explanation: The preterite of 'estar' plus 'durante' frames the closure as a completed stretch. It does not imply an ongoing state.

provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Use the imperfect for background description
questions.stem: Which sentence best describes the scene while a meeting happened?

options.text: 'The room became bright and the windows opened.'
'The room was bright and the windows were open.'

questions.explanation: The imperfect describes ongoing background conditions. The other options mark changes or use the wrong aspect.

questions.stem: In a memo, 'Quería pedirle un favor' softens the request. What sense does the imperfect add?
questions.explanation: The imperfect of querer softens the request into a polite, conditional tone. It does not mean habit or completion.
